co_colorado_springs.blurb: Climbing around Colorado Springs is scattered through parks, canyons and ridges on the edge of the city, beneath a 14,000-foot peak whose weather can differ sharply from places farther north. Bouldering, trad and sport are close to evenly split, with a little ice, mixed and alpine on the side. Roped grades are mostly 5.9 to 5.11, and boulder problems run from beginner level up to hard. Garden of the Gods and Red Rock Canyon Open Space are red sandstone; North Cheyenne Canyon has granite walls in side canyons, mostly sport with some trad and winter ice. Old Stage Road is the busiest sub-area for trad and sport, while Ute Valley Park is mostly boulders.

va_central_southern_va_region.blurb: This grouping covers climbing around Charlottesville, Richmond and the Lynchburg area, and it is overwhelmingly a bouldering region. Problems start at the easiest grades and reach hard ones, with the bulk in the V0 to V6 band, while a smaller number of trad, sport and top-rope lines fill out the rest, mostly moderate up to 5.11. Charlottesville vicinity holds the most climbs, and the Blue Ridge Parkway has a large concentration of greenstone boulders. In Richmond the climbing sits in urban and riverside parks along the James: the Buttermilks for boulders, Belle Isle mostly for top-ropes, Browns Island for sport, and Manchester Wall, built from the leftover pillars of an old bridge, for both trad and sport.

nh_rumney.blurb: Rumney is a sport climbing destination spread over many crags on the hillside of Rattlesnake Mountain, above the town of Rumney in New Hampshire. Everything is schist, with a visible grain, and lines tend to follow aretes, grooves, dikes, corners and cracks rather than blank faces. Sport routes dominate, with a solid amount of trad and a large bouldering area. Grades run from beginner level to the very hardest, but the heart of the climbing is 5.10 to 5.12, so there is plenty for strong climbers and a fair choice of moderates. Fall is the peak season. Main Cliff, The Meadows and Rumney Bouldering are among the largest sub-areas.

wa_index.blurb: Index is a small village on the Skykomish River, just north of Highway 2, with steep granite walls rising above it. The Upper Town Wall is close to 600 feet and nearly vertical, the Lower Town Wall is shorter with a steeper middle, and a dozen or so smaller crags sit in the woods, mostly facing south. Trad and sport are about equally common, and bouldering on large granite blocks is good too. Most roped climbing falls between 5.10 and 5.12, though a healthy number of 5.9 and easier lines exist. Low elevation and southern exposure mean routes dry out after a few dry days in winter, but rain leaves many seeping, and the big walls get hot in summer. Passing trains are loud.

wy_vedauwoo.blurb: Vedauwoo lies in southeast Wyoming, north of Interstate 80 between Laramie and Cheyenne, in the Pole Mountain area of the Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest. The rock is coarse Sherman Granite roughly 1.4 billion years old, weathered into hoodoos, domes, towers and boulders. It is best known for crack climbing, especially offwidths, and trad dominates, with a good bouldering scene and only a little sport. Most roped lines fall between 5.6 and 5.11, concentrated around 5.10, with climbs running up to about three pitches. Some crags sit close to the road while others are more remote and quiet. Most formations have walk-offs, though rappel bolts are common. Blair, Nautilus and Reynolds Hill are the biggest sub-areas.

_expect.name: Denver Metropolitan Area Bouldering and Buildering

co_denver_metropolitan_area_bouldering_a.blurb: This is the urban side of Denver climbing: short problems, artificial walls and buildings across the metro area, plus one larger natural zone to the south. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, mainly V0 to V6, with some sport, trad and top-rope lines on top. Denver South, centred on Castle Rock at about 6,200 feet, is by far the biggest sub-area, with rocks and boulders in small gorges that act as sun traps and stay warm on cold winter days. In the city itself, the University of Denver campus has buildering, and Central Park has a low artificial wall with problems from V0 to V8. Downtown Denver and the 5 Points neighbourhood offer buildering on structures.
